blocks.text: In a healthy animal the internal tissues, such as blood, brain and muscle, are normally free of microorganisms. The surface tissues, such as the skin and the mucous membranes, are constantly in contact with the environment and are colonised by certain microbial species. The mixture of organisms regularly found at any anatomical site is called the normal flora.

blocks.title: Normal flora
blocks.text: The mixture of microorganisms regularly found at a particular site of the body, such as the skin, the mouth or the intestine. In humans it consists of bacteria, a few fungi and protists, and some methanogenic archaea; bacteria are its most numerous and obvious members.

The association between humans and their normal flora is mutualistic: both sides benefit. In the human body the normal flora gets nutrients, a stable environment, a constant temperature, protection and transport. The body, in turn, gets several benefits from its normal bacteria.
Benefits of the bacterial flora of humans

items: Synthesis of vitamins: bacteria in the alimentary canal produce vitamins and excrete those in excess of their needs. These vitamins are absorbed from the alimentary canal and distributed in the body. Enteric bacteria secrete vitamin K and vitamin B12, and lactic acid bacteria produce certain B vitamins.
Prevention of colonisation by pathogens: the bacteria of the normal flora compete with pathogens for attachment sites and nutrients, so pathogens have less chance of entering body tissues.
Inhibiting or killing pathogens: the intestinal bacteria produce a variety of substances that inhibit or kill pathogenic bacteria.

Stimulation of cross-reactive antibodies: because the normal flora behaves as antigens, it induces an immunological response. Low levels of antibodies produced against the normal flora are known to cross-react with certain pathogens and thereby prevent infection or invasion.
